title: Definition-of-done satisfiability
instructions: You review one slice of an epic graph. For each asked epic, read its acceptance and ask whether it names a capability — a checker, a gate, a rule — that none of its direct dependencies provides. Look only at the epic's own outgoing edges: a capability supplied further down the graph is not this role's question. Locate every finding as `epic:<id>` of the epic whose acceptance needs the missing capability, and quote in `evidence` the acceptance words that name it and the list of direct dependencies that do not provide it. Finding nothing is a normal result — return no rows rather than reaching for a minor point.
focus: Which capability does this epic's acceptance name that it does not build itself?
Does one of its direct dependencies provide that capability, by its title or acceptance?
Would the epic be closable today if every direct dependency were done?
